title: Designing Flow: Building the identity of Zip Forward 2026
summary: How Zip’s brand team brought the Zip Forward 2026 identity to life, from the stage to a Hudson River 5K.
body_markdown:
## Zip Forward began in motion.


On a warm September afternoon along the Hudson River, more than a hundred members of the Zip Community set out on a 5K path, opening a week built around a single idea: flow state.


The run ended at a pop-up newsstand, a nod to the city around us and an invitation for New Yorkers to stop by for free coffee, food, and snacks, along with the first edition of The Forward Edition, a newspaper filled with ideas for working in flow.


For Zip Forward, we wanted to bring these ideas somewhere new.


To work today means balancing new systems, AI tools, and teams all moving at once. The question isn't just how work moves, but how people stay focused while it does. And when everything starts working together, the friction falls away; the pieces begin to move as one. Work becomes more focused, more intuitive, and more effortless.


That's flow state. It was a natural evolution of what ‘flow’ has always meant at Zip, and a bigger vision towards where we're headed.


## How to visualize a feeling.


Flow began as the theme, but Zip Forward was a physical experience, so the identity had to carry through every touchpoint, from programming and product messaging to brand activations. It was a design concept that needed to be felt in every piece.


We started with the feeling itself: when complexity falls away until only clarity remains.


This became the visual idea at the center of the identity. Shapes soften at their edges and dissolve through diffusion. Gradients ripple outward, moving from layered to focused. Nothing snaps into place. Everything transitions.


Our moodboard followed the same logic. We looked at soft light, translucent materials that filter and blur without ever fully blocking what sits behind them. We were drawn to things that felt atmospheric rather than rigid, where one thing could naturally become another.


## That thinking extended beyond the screen.


On stage, colored light moved from one hue into the next, bringing the same sense of diffusion into the room. The stage itself became part of the identity, carrying the visual language through the keynote and giving the on-screen motion a physical backdrop.


Motion became one of the most important parts of the system. The identity wasn't meant to sit still; gradients moved, forms dissolved, and layers shifted in and out of focus. The movement gave the visuals the quality that a static identity couldn't: a sense that everything was already in motion.


And then we took the idea off the screen entirely.


Inside the venue, we created a Flow Zone, an open space where attendees could step away for guided meditation, sound baths, or simply a quieter moment. Throughout the programming, we kept coming back to the same question: *what does it mean to work in flow when the technology, processes, and systems around you are designed to work together?*


Flow State became more than the look of Zip Forward. It became a way of thinking about the entire experience, from the first mile of the run to the last session on stage, all the way to the saxophone player weaving through the space as the evening came to a close. **** (Yes, we leaned all in.)


##
Reflections


Events are a powerful design medium because they give an idea somewhere to live.


You can give it a physical space, a sound, a rhythm, a point of view. You can let people interact with it instead of simply looking at it. You have the rare opportunity to bring every expression of a brand together in one place.


That’s what we were after with Flow State. We didn’t want the idea to live only in the identity, but to show up in the way people moved throughout the event; what they saw, what they heard, and how they experienced the brand.


In that sense, Zip Forward has become more than an event for us. It’s become a flagship moment for the company, and a kind of proving ground for how we think about the bigger moments we create throughout the year. Product launches, campaigns, customer moments, company initiatives: increasingly, we think about all of these through the same lens. **‍**


## It’s the ability to tell a story in more than one dimension.
